title: Brownian motion: mean square displacement
caption: In three dimensions ⟨r²⟩ = 6Dt, so with D = 2 × 10⁻¹³ m² s⁻¹ the particle's mean square displacement grows linearly, 1.2 μm² per second, reaching 12.0 μm² (1.2e-11 m²) after 10 s: an rms distance of 3.5 μm. Linear growth in t (not t²) is what separates diffusion from steady drift.
alt: Straight line through the origin: mean square displacement against time, reaching 12.0 square micrometres at 10 seconds.
description: The horizontal axis is time in seconds; the vertical axis is ⟨r²⟩ in μm².
⟨r²⟩ = 6Dt is a straight line with gradient 6D = 1.2 μm² s⁻¹.
At t = 10 s: ⟨r²⟩ = 12.0 μm², so r_rms = 3.5 μm.
